title: October 11, 1902: a boy was born in a river-island village who would spend his life arguing for power to stay close to the people.
caption:
October 11, 1902: a boy was born in a river-island village who would spend his life arguing for power to stay close to the people.

He went on to become one of India's most prominent freedom-struggle leaders, drawn early to the Sarvodaya philosophy of Gandhi and Vinoba Bhave - the idea that real progress means uplift reaching everyone, not just those already close to power.

Known to many simply as 'JP,' he championed grassroots self-governance and civil liberties as the real measure of a free society - work that earned him the honorific 'Lok Nayak,' people's leader and a posthumous Bharat Ratna in 1999.

His Sarvodaya-rooted vision of grassroots democracy remains a live question for any nation still working out how development reaches its furthest corners.
